referenceContextActuallyViewed.purpose: Existing preserved comparison used only to observe near-white moving interface; not reference-equivalent approval

observations.whiteCore: At every sampled same-frame comparison, the new near-white/cream core is visibly brighter and easier to trace than the Parent amber divider. It remains narrow and follows the existing irregular material boundary.
observations.warmHalo: A subdued warm shoulder is visible around the sharper core in the larger comparison images. Its spread remains local; it does not wash either territory body into yellow or produce a broad neon band.
observations.continuousCoRegistration: Across all 150 contact thumbnails, the emphasized edge advances with the orange-purple ownership interface. No separated trail, detached duplicate, obvious gap or abrupt flash is visible at this review scale. The same-frame comparisons place it on the same interface as Parent.
observations.colorSeparation: Orange and purple remain distinct on either side of the core throughout the sequence. Terrain relief and blue sea remain readable, and the local warm glow does not conceal the territory color distinction.
observations.mobileReadability: The core remains traceable even in the small contact-sheet portrait tiles and is clearer than Parent in the scaled side-by-side panels. This supports improved readability for a portrait/mobile presentation; no physical phone, display-brightness or video-app playback test was performed.
observations.iconOcclusion: National flag badges remain legible and separate from the frontier. No new glow coverage, badge disappearance or broad illumination over badge faces is visible in the reviewed sequence or sampled comparisons.
observations.noExtraLines: No new route, arrow, decorative front, outer national outline or other standalone line is visible. The added emphasis belongs to the current orange-purple interface. Review headings and footers are outside the movie panels.
observations.preservedContent: Same-frame comparisons show matching camera composition, terrain, sea, ownership colors, coast geometry and national badge placement outside the narrow frontier neighborhood. Exact equality is corroborated only by the separate three-frame raw measurement evidence and focused tests.
observations.sequenceStart: Frames 0-29 show a readable bright edge across the peninsula, including short western fragments; no start flash is visible in these thumbnails.
observations.sequenceMiddle: Frames 30-119 show the jagged edge advancing northward while the camera tracks. The core stays present through the changes in shape and framing.
observations.sequenceEnd: Frames 120-149 keep a visible bright edge at the advancing frontier. No terminal disappearance is expected because the locked public excerpt continues advancing.
observations.referenceContext: The inspected reference panel has a sharp near-white advancing interface. The new core moves toward that contrast treatment. Its extensive gold outer borders, contact pips, other materials and icon style were not copied or graded as part of this glow-only review.
observations.remainingStyleLimit: The inherited frontier remains visibly angular at several bends, especially the middle and end checkpoints. That shape is unchanged in the Parent comparison and does not require a geometry change within the authorized glow-only scope.

measurementCorrection.cause: Original geometric mask assumed Euclidean distance to finite polyline segments. The immutable shader uses a latitude scalar field normalised by native 2x2 quad derivatives, then presentation bilinear sampling. Every previously flagged coordinate is independently explained by that exact existing kernel.

methodLimits: Three actual static frames, not a 150-frame raw-pixel equality claim.
Parent raw NORMAL includes halo; parent width is combined-highlight FWHM, not isolated core width.
Half-pixel canvas-centre and quarter-pixel bilinear samples; PNG is original output, not reencoded.
Land-interior midpoint profile samples are reused with all original scene/PNG hashes reverified; they exclude badges, coast clipping and knot derivative discontinuities.
The corrected support mask comes only from immutable field uniforms, native quad derivatives and the existing presentation inverse/sampler; it is not derived from changed output pixels.
Unchanged GIS rasterisation/filter support retains its original 3px budget; strict field support remains exactly profile 10px.
Outside support equality uses raw PNG; lossy H264 can change decoded pixels beyond the light support.

correctionProvenance.reviewScope: First Euclidean-mask failure remains preserved; the corrected verification mask is source-derived native 2x2 quad/bilinear support. No shader/profile change or support-tolerance increase is claimed.

limitations: All 150 encoded frames were visually inspected only as chronological contact thumbnails; five sampled frames were inspected in larger comparisons. This does not certify every individual output pixel or high-frequency playback behavior.
No real-time MP4 playback or browser/GPU interactive playback was performed by this reviewer; absence of subtle temporal flicker is not certified.

The 5-second public excerpt advances throughout. It contains no actual stop and cannot demonstrate stop fade without changing the locked timeline. The private 4/4 focused-test record reports a monotone 12-frame settle to strength 0.08, but no rendered private stop was visually reviewed here.

Widths, luminance gains and exact raw protection are quoted from separately preserved actual raw measurements at frames 0, 74 and 149; they are not a 150-frame raw equality proof or measurements from the resized comparison panels.
Raw outside-support and badge equality do not establish decoded H264 bit equality outside the support; lossy encoding can affect neighboring decoded pixels.
Mobile readability is a scaled-image judgment, not a physical-device or mobile-video-app test.

Reference context consists of one preserved source-frame-235 comparison panel. No complete reference movie review, whole-world-map quality approval or reference-equivalent quality approval is claimed.
recommendation: Retain this candidate as an improved moving-frontier-glow-only result and stop at USER_VIDEO_REVIEW_REQUIRED. No source, scene, media or geometry rework is requested by this scoped review.
